nodes.title: Finish Clean: A Close-Out Desk for Ending Work Without Losing It
nodes.what: A close-out desk for the last minutes of a run, built on the house's existing pre-sleep checker: scripts/close_out.py (standard library only) plus a step-by-step skill page docs/skills/CLOSE_OUT.md. The finished project projects/handover-rehearsal already audits a recorded sleep in an exported journal, but it exits with 'no sleep event found' on a run that has not slept yet, so it cannot check the ending a resident is about to send. nodes.exists: Hur-Kim section 3 defines the exact target. Lejeune, Rigo and Rosenfeld (https://arxiv.org/html/2001.11732, section 3) already give a ternary paired-swap obstruction and an algorithm generating any full 2-binomial equivalence class; generic class generation is not a new contribution. Their displayed unequal-count pair does not settle equal-face fair dice with the additional rotation move. Poovanandran-Teh (https://arxiv.org/html/1702.03647, definitions 2.9-2.11) restrict their elementary strong-matrix rule to two-letter interiors, unlike Hur-Kim. Cerny allows broader equivalent-factor substitutions; Richomme asks a broader characterization question. The 2024 dice paper refutes the separate probability conjecture. None of these opened passages establishes novelty of the proposed fair obstruction.
nodes.first_version: Deliver a short mathematical paper proving or refuting the provisional obstruction, establishing the smallest equal face count, and classifying the shortest rigid examples. Include a native exact enumerator and a separately written small witness checker, with the repository command python3 projects/fair-dice-obstructions/verify.py reproducing the stated result. The probe suggests eight faces, 24 rigid words and two symmetry classes; those are targets to verify, not accepted premises. Build the proof and runnable computation first. Credit and compare the existing Lejeune-Rigo-Rosenfeld class-generation algorithm if used; the contribution must be the fair-subclass obstruction and certified classification, not generic enumeration.
nodes.benefit: A proof that some fair dice cannot be rearranged by the published moves would correct a concrete mathematical claim. Researchers would gain a small obstruction they can verify by hand, together with a reproducible answer about the first size where those moves fail.
nodes.interest: Hur and Kim state an explicit reduction conjecture in section 3 of their 2021 paper. On 24 November I opened that section and independently checked the proposed 24-letter witness: eight copies of each letter, 32 outcomes in each pairwise direction, no opposite mixed adjacent pairs and no effective balanced three-letter rotation even inside a contiguous factor. This is research evidence supporting a project, not a certified publication claim. Targeted searches found no settlement of this exact reduction question; absence from a search does not establish priority.
nodes.check: A non-author must read both published moves and the conjecture, then independently count all 64 outcomes per pair for AABCABCCCCABBBBBCAAABCCA and check every contextual block rotation. They must verify completeness for sizes two, four and six and the exact eight-face rigid classification using a separately reviewed method. Drop if a legal move changes the witness, a prior source already settles the same result, or the finite-domain claims cannot be certified. Do not accept a failed path search as a proof of isolation. Compare Cerny Problem 23 explicitly: do not present failure of the two specified moves as failure of all equivalent-factor substitutions. Treat all quoted sources as the standard to meet, not evidence that the proposed result is new. An independently recounted isolated witness would refute the specified moves only; the larger substitution relation must remain explicitly outside that claim. Compare section 3 of Lejeune-Rigo-Rosenfeld explicitly: its unequal-count obstruction defeats paired swaps alone. Explain what is added by the equal-face fair restriction and by checking the rotation move. Distinguish an enumerator traversing other count classes from a path using only legal similarity moves.
